npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا. مَاذَا تُرِيدُ؟
npc.en: Good evening! Welcome. What would you like?

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور! أُرِيدُ شَايًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Good evening! I would like a tea, please.
choices.feedback: Good: مَسَاءُ النُّور answers مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر, and شَايًا takes -an as the object of أُرِيدُ.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور! أُرِيدُ قَهْوَةً، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Good evening! I would like a coffee, please.
choices.feedback: Good: a coffee instead of tea. قَهْوَةً takes -an as the object.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور! أُرِيدُ شَايًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.
choices.en: Good evening! I would like a tea, please (to a woman).
choices.feedback: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ (-ki) is for a woman. The waiter is a man: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (-ka).

npc.ar: شَاي بِالنَّعْنَاع أَوْ شَاي عَادِيّ؟
npc.en: Tea with mint, or ordinary tea?

choices.ar: بِالنَّعْنَاع، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، وَبِدُونِ سُكَّر.
choices.en: With mint, please, and without sugar.
choices.feedback: Clear and polite: you choose one of the two and add how you take it.

choices.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Yes, please.
choices.feedback: He asks 'this or that?' (أَوْ), so 'yes' does not answer. Choose one: بِالنَّعْنَاع or عَادِيّ.

npc.ar: قَهْوَة بِسُكَّر أَوْ بِدُونِ سُكَّر؟
npc.en: Coffee with sugar or without sugar?

choices.ar: بِسُكَّر قَلِيل، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: With a little sugar, please.
choices.feedback: Good: قَلِيل follows the noun, like every adjective.

choices.ar: بِسُكَّر كَثِيرَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: With a lot of sugar, please (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: سُكَّر is masculine, so the adjective has no ة: بِسُكَّر كَثِير.

npc.ar: حَاضِر! هَلْ تُرِيدُ شَيْئًا آخَر؟ عِنْدَنَا كَعْك طَازَج.
npc.en: Certainly! Would you like anything else? We have fresh cake.

choices.ar: نَعَم، قِطْعَةَ كَعْك وَاحِدَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Yes, one piece of cake, please.
choices.feedback: Good: قِطْعَة is feminine, so 'one' is وَاحِدَة, after the noun.

choices.ar: لَا، شُكْرًا. هٰذَا كُلُّ شَيْء.
choices.en: No, thank you. That's everything.
choices.feedback: Polite and complete: a 'no' with شُكْرًا is never rude.

choices.ar: نَعَم، قِطْعَةَ كَعْك وَاحِد، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Yes, one piece of cake, please (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: 'One' agrees with قِطْعَة, which is feminine: قِطْعَةَ كَعْك وَاحِدَة.

npc.ar: تَفَضَّلْ. بِالْهَنَاء وَالشِّفَاء!
npc.en: Here you are. Enjoy!

choices.ar: شُكْرًا! وَمِنْ فَضْلِكَ، كَمِ الْحِسَاب؟
choices.en: Thank you! And please, how much is the bill?
choices.feedback: Good: before al- the sukūn of كَمْ becomes i, كَمِ الْحِسَاب (kami l-ḥisāb).

choices.ar: شُكْرًا! هَاتِ الْحِسَاب!
choices.en: Thanks! Give me the bill!
choices.feedback: هَاتِ (give!) with no 'please' sounds like an order to a waiter. Ask politely: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، كَمِ الْحِسَاب؟

npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! إِلَى أَيْنَ؟
npc.en: Good evening! Where to?

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور! إِلَى الْمَتْحَف الْمِصْرِيّ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Good evening! To the Egyptian Museum, please.
choices.feedback: Good: مَسَاءُ النُّور answers مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر, and إِلَى + the place is all a driver needs.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور! إِلَى الْمَتْحَف الْمِصْرِيّ، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.
choices.en: Good evening! To the Egyptian Museum, please (to a woman).
choices.feedback: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ (-ki) is for a woman. The driver is a man: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (-ka).

npc.ar: الْمَتْحَف قَرِيب، فِي مَيْدَانِ التَّحْرِير.
npc.en: The museum is close, on Tahrir Square.

choices.ar: كَمِ الْأُجْرَة إِلَى الْمَتْحَف، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: How much is the fare to the museum, please?
choices.feedback: Wise: agree on the fare before you set off. Before al- the sukūn of كَمْ becomes i: كَمِ الْأُجْرَة.

choices.ar: كَمْ أُجْرَة إِلَى الْمَتْحَف، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: How much fare to the museum, please? (missing 'the')
choices.feedback: You ask about 'the fare' for this ride, so use الـ: كَمِ الْأُجْرَة؟ The m of كَمْ takes an i to link to it.

npc.ar: خَمْسُونَ جُنَيْهًا. الطَّرِيق مُزْدَحِم الْيَوْم.
npc.en: Fifty pounds. The road is crowded today.

choices.ar: خَمْسُونَ كَثِير! أَرْبَعُونَ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: Fifty is a lot! How about forty, please?
choices.feedback: Polite bargaining: a lower number with مِنْ فَضْلِكَ, as a question.

choices.ar: طَيِّب، خَمْسُونَ جُنَيْهًا.
choices.en: OK, fifty pounds.
choices.feedback: Fine too: you accept the fare. After fifty the noun is singular with -an: جُنَيْهًا.

choices.ar: طَيِّب، خَمْسُونَ جُنَيْهَات.
choices.en: OK, fifty pounds (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: After 11 to 99 the noun is singular with the ending -an: خَمْسُونَ جُنَيْهًا.

npc.ar: طَيِّب، أَرْبَعُونَ. تَفَضَّلِي!
npc.en: OK, forty then. Please get in!

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا!
choices.en: Thank you very much!
choices.feedback: Good: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا is a fixed formula, so جَزِيلًا keeps its -an.

choices.ar: عَفْوًا!
choices.en: You're welcome!
choices.feedback: عَفْوًا answers a thank-you. The driver agreed to your price, so you thank him: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا!

npc.ar: هَلْ أَذْهَبُ يَمِينًا هُنَا أَوْ يَسَارًا؟
npc.en: Do I go right here, or left?

choices.ar: يَمِينًا، ثُمَّ إِلَى الْأَمَام، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Right, and then straight ahead, please.
choices.feedback: Good: 'go right' is يَمِينًا, with the adverb ending -an.

choices.ar: يَمِين، ثُمَّ إِلَى الْأَمَام، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Right, and then straight ahead, please (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: يَمِين is the noun 'right side'. To say 'go right', it takes -an: يَمِينًا.

choices.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Yes, please.
choices.feedback: He asks 'right or left?' (أَوْ), so 'yes' does not answer. Choose one: يَمِينًا or يَسَارًا.

npc.ar: هٰذَا هُوَ الْمَتْحَف الْمِصْرِيّ. وَصَلْنَا!
npc.en: This is the Egyptian Museum. We have arrived!

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! تَفَضَّلْ، الْأُجْرَة. مَعَ السَّلَامَة!
choices.en: Thank you very much! Here you are, the fare. Goodbye!
choices.feedback: Good: تَفَضَّلْ (no ending) is 'here you are' to a man.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! تَفَضَّلِي، الْأُجْرَة. مَعَ السَّلَامَة!
choices.en: Thank you very much! Here you are (to a woman), the fare. Goodbye!
choices.feedback: The driver said تَفَضَّلِي to you because you are a woman. To him, a man, say تَفَضَّلْ.

npc.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا فَيْصَل! كَيْفَ حَالُكَ الْيَوْم؟
npc.en: Good morning, Faisal! How are you today?

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور يَا خَالَة هُدَى! أَنَا بِخَيْر، الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه.
choices.en: Good morning, Auntie Huda! I am fine, thank God.
segs: aunt (polite address for an older woman)
choices.feedback: Good: صَبَاحُ النُّور answers صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر, and يَا خَالَة is a warm, polite way to address an older woman.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور! أَنَا بِخَيْر. وَكَيْفَ حَالُكَ يَا خَالَة؟
choices.en: Good morning! I am fine. And how are you, Auntie? (wrong ending)
segs: aunt (polite address for an older woman)
choices.feedback: Asking back is kind, but حَالُكَ (-ka) is for a man. Huda is a woman: وَكَيْفَ حَالُكِ (-ki)؟

npc.ar: مَتَى تَسْتَيْقِظُ عَادَةً؟ أَنَا أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة.
npc.en: When do you usually wake up? I wake up at six o'clock.

choices.ar: أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف، ثُمَّ أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي.
choices.en: I wake up at half past six, then I wash my face.
choices.feedback: Good: she asks تَسْتَيْقِظُ (you wake up) and you answer with أَسْتَيْقِظُ (I wake up).

choices.ar: تَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف.
choices.en: You wake up at half past six (wrong person).
choices.feedback: You copied the question's verb. Talking about yourself, the verb starts with أَ: أَسْتَيْقِظُ (I wake up).

npc.ar: وَمَاذَا تَشْرَبُ فِي الصَّبَاح؟ شَاي أَوْ قَهْوَة؟
npc.en: And what do you drink in the morning? Tea or coffee?

choices.ar: أَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ، بِدُونِ سُكَّر.
choices.en: I drink coffee, please, without sugar.
choices.feedback: Good: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ with -ki, because you are speaking to a woman.

choices.ar: أَشْرَبُ الشَّاي، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ، بِدُونِ سُكَّر.
choices.en: I drink tea, please, without sugar.
choices.feedback: Good: tea instead of coffee, and -ki in مِنْ فَضْلِكِ for a woman.

choices.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.
choices.en: Yes, please.
choices.feedback: She asks 'tea or coffee?' (أَوْ), so 'yes' does not answer. Choose one: أَشْرَبُ الشَّاي or أَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَة.

npc.ar: حَاضِر. وَالْفُطُور؟ عِنْدِي فُول وَخُبْز وَبَيْض.
npc.en: Right away. And breakfast? I have beans, bread and eggs.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا خَالَة، لٰكِنْ أَنَا لَا آكُلُ كَثِيرًا فِي الصَّبَاح.
choices.en: Thank you, Auntie, but I don't eat much in the morning.
segs: aunt (polite address for an older woman)
choices.feedback: Polite: thanks first, then لٰكِنْ. And لَا comes straight before the verb: لَا آكُلُ.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا خَالَة! أُرِيدُ فُولًا وَخُبْزًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.
choices.en: Thank you, Auntie! I would like beans and bread, please.
segs: aunt (polite address for an older woman)
choices.feedback: Good: both things are objects of أُرِيدُ, so both take -an: فُولًا وَخُبْزًا.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا خَالَة، لٰكِنْ لَا أَنَا آكُلُ كَثِيرًا فِي الصَّبَاح.
choices.en: Thank you, Auntie, but I don't eat much in the morning (wrong word order).
segs: aunt (polite address for an older woman)
choices.feedback: لَا goes directly before the verb, not before the pronoun: أَنَا لَا آكُلُ كَثِيرًا.

npc.ar: لَا، لَا! الْفُطُور مُهِمّ. كُلْ قَلِيلًا عَلَى الْأَقَلّ!
npc.en: No, no! Breakfast is important. At least eat a little!

choices.ar: حَاضِر! قَلِيلًا مِنَ الْفُول، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.
choices.en: All right! A little of the beans, please.
choices.feedback: Good: حَاضِر is a friendly 'all right!', and قَلِيلًا مِنَ الْفُول is 'a little of the beans'.

choices.ar: حَاضِر! قَلِيلًا مِنَ الْفُول، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: All right! A little of the beans, please (to a man).
choices.feedback: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (-ka) is for a man. To Huda, a woman: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ (-ki).

npc.ar: وَمَتَى تَخْرُجُ إِلَى الدَّرْس؟
npc.en: And when do you leave for the lesson?
segs: you go out, you leave (to a man)

choices.ar: أَخْرُجُ فِي السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة، لِأَنَّ الدَّرْسَ فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة.
choices.en: I leave at eight o'clock, because the lesson is at nine.
choices.feedback: Good: you answer تَخْرُجُ with أَخْرُجُ (I leave), and each hour is a feminine ordinal: الثَّامِنَة، التَّاسِعَة. After لِأَنَّ the noun ends in -a: الدَّرْسَ.

choices.ar: أَخْرُجُ فِي السَّاعَة الثَّامِن، لِأَنَّ الدَّرْسَ فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة.
choices.en: I leave at eight o'clock, because the lesson is at nine (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: سَاعَة is feminine, so the ordinal after it takes ة: السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة.

npc.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر، هٰذَا مَكْتَبُ الْمَدْرَسَة. كَيْفَ أُسَاعِدُكَ؟
npc.en: Good morning, this is the school office. How can I help you?

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أَنَا فَيْصَل، طَالِب فِي صَفِّ الْأُسْتَاذ كَرِيم. أُرِيدُ مَوْعِدًا مَعَ الْمُدِير.
choices.en: Good morning. I am Faisal, a student in Mr Karim's class. I would like an appointment with the director.
choices.feedback: Clear: who you are, then what you want. مَوْعِدًا takes -an as the object of أُرِيدُ.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ مَوْعِد مَعَ الْمُدِير.
choices.en: Good morning. I would like an appointment with the director (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: The object of أُرِيدُ takes -an: أُرِيدُ مَوْعِدًا مَعَ الْمُدِير.

npc.ar: طَبْعًا. هَلْ يَوْمُ الثُّلَاثَاء مُمْكِن، فِي السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة؟
npc.en: Of course. Is Tuesday possible, at ten o'clock?

choices.ar: نَعَم، يَوْمُ الثُّلَاثَاء مُمْكِن.
choices.en: Yes, Tuesday is possible.
choices.feedback: Good: يَوْم is masculine, so 'possible' has no ة: مُمْكِن.

choices.ar: آسِف، يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاء فِي السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة عِنْدِي دَرْس.
choices.en: Sorry, on Tuesday at ten o'clock I have a lesson.
choices.feedback: Good: آسِف (m) because you are a man, and 'on Tuesday' is يَوْمَ, with -a.

choices.ar: نَعَم، يَوْمُ الثُّلَاثَاء مُمْكِنَة.
choices.en: Yes, Tuesday is possible (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: يَوْم is masculine, so 'possible' has no ة: يَوْمُ الثُّلَاثَاء مُمْكِن.

npc.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة. وَيَوْمَ الْأَرْبِعَاء؟ الْمُدِير هُنَا مِنَ السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة إِلَى السَّاعَة الرَّابِعَة.
npc.en: No problem. And on Wednesday? The director is here from one o'clock to four o'clock.

choices.ar: الْأَرْبِعَاء مُمْتَاز. هَلِ السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة وَالنِّصْف مُمْكِنَة؟
choices.en: Wednesday is great. Is half past one possible?
choices.feedback: Good: السَّاعَة is feminine, so 'possible' takes ة: مُمْكِنَة. Before al- هَلْ becomes هَلِ.

choices.ar: الْأَرْبِعَاء مُمْتَاز. هَلِ السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة وَالنِّصْف مُمْكِن؟
choices.en: Wednesday is great. Is half past one possible? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: سَاعَة is feminine, so 'possible' takes ة: هَلِ السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة وَالنِّصْف مُمْكِنَة؟

npc.ar: آسِفَة، فِي السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة وَالنِّصْف عِنْدَهُ اِجْتِمَاع. هَلِ السَّاعَة الثَّالِثَة إِلَّا رُبْعًا مُمْكِنَة لَكَ؟
npc.en: Sorry, at half past one he has a meeting. Is quarter to three possible for you?

choices.ar: نَعَم، هٰذَا وَقْت مُمْتَاز. الدَّرْس حَتَّى السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة فَقَطْ.
choices.en: Yes, that is an excellent time. The lesson only goes on until one o'clock.
choices.feedback: Good: وَقْت is masculine, so هٰذَا and مُمْتَاز have no ة.

choices.ar: نَعَم، هٰذِهِ وَقْت مُمْتَاز.
choices.en: Yes, that is an excellent time (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: وَقْت is masculine, so 'this' is هٰذَا: نَعَم، هٰذَا وَقْت مُمْتَاز.

npc.ar: إِذًا، مَوْعِدُكَ يَوْمَ الْأَرْبِعَاء فِي السَّاعَة الثَّالِثَة إِلَّا رُبْعًا.
npc.en: So, your appointment is on Wednesday at quarter to three.

choices.ar: الْأَرْبِعَاء، الثَّالِثَة إِلَّا رُبْعًا. شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا أُسْتَاذَة! مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Wednesday, quarter to three. Thank you very much, madam! Goodbye.
choices.feedback: Good: repeating the day and time checks you understood, and يَا أُسْتَاذَة is polite to a woman.

choices.ar: الْأَرْبِعَاء، الثَّالِثَة إِلَّا رُبْعًا. شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا أُسْتَاذ! مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Wednesday, quarter to three. Thank you very much, sir! Goodbye.
segs: Mr, sir (polite address for a man)
choices.feedback: يَا أُسْتَاذ is for a man. The receptionist is a woman: يَا أُسْتَاذَة.

npc.ar: إِذًا، مَوْعِدُكَ يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاء فِي السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة.
npc.en: So, your appointment is on Tuesday at ten o'clock.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا أُسْتَاذَة! مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much, madam! Goodbye.
choices.feedback: Good: يَا أُسْتَاذَة is a polite way to address a woman you do not know.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا أُسْتَاذَة! أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا.
choices.en: Thank you very much, madam! Welcome.
choices.feedback: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا welcomes someone who arrives. You are leaving, so say goodbye: مَعَ السَّلَامَة.

npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! أَهْلًا بِكُمَا فِي مَطْعَمِنَا. كَمْ شَخْصًا؟
npc.en: Good evening! Welcome to our restaurant. How many people?

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور! نَحْنُ شَخْصَانِ: أَنَا وَصَدِيقِي. طَاوِلَة لِاثْنَيْنِ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Good evening! There are two of us: me and my friend. A table for two, please.
choices.feedback: Good: after نَحْنُ the dual is the predicate, so it ends in -āni: شَخْصَانِ. After لِ it is -ayni: لِاثْنَيْنِ.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور! نَحْنُ شَخْصَيْنِ: أَنَا وَصَدِيقِي.
choices.en: Good evening! There are two of us: me and my friend (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: After نَحْنُ the dual is the predicate, not an object, so it ends in -āni: نَحْنُ شَخْصَانِ.

npc.ar: تَفَضَّلَا، هٰذِهِ طَاوِلَة جَمِيلَة بِجَانِبِ النَّافِذَة. وَهٰذِهِ الْقَائِمَة.
npc.en: Please sit down, here is a nice table by the window. And here is the menu.
segs: please, here you are (to two people)

choices.ar: شُكْرًا. مَا هٰذَا الطَّبَق؟ هَلْ فِيهِ لَحْم؟
choices.en: Thank you. What is this dish? Is there meat in it?
choices.feedback: Good: طَبَق is masculine, so 'this' is هٰذَا and 'in it' is فِيهِ.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا. مَا هٰذِهِ الطَّبَق؟ هَلْ فِيهِ لَحْم؟
choices.en: Thank you. What is this dish? Is there meat in it? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: طَبَق is masculine, so 'this' is هٰذَا: مَا هٰذَا الطَّبَق؟

npc.ar: هٰذِهِ مُلُوخِيَّة بِالدَّجَاج. وَعِنْدَنَا أَيْضًا مَحْشِيّ بِدُونِ لَحْم.
npc.en: This is molokhia with chicken. We also have stuffed vegetables without meat.

choices.ar: إِذًا نُرِيدُ طَبَقَيْنِ مِنَ الْمَحْشِيّ، وَسَلَطَةً خَضْرَاء، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Then we'd like two plates of stuffed vegetables and a green salad, please.
choices.feedback: Good: as the object of نُرِيدُ the dual ends in -ayni (طَبَقَيْنِ), and سَلَطَةً takes -an.

choices.ar: إِذًا نُرِيدُ طَبَقَانِ مِنَ الْمَحْشِيّ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Then we'd like two plates of stuffed vegetables, please (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: As the object of a verb the dual ends in -ayni, not -āni: نُرِيدُ طَبَقَيْنِ مِنَ الْمَحْشِيّ.

npc.ar: وَمَاذَا تَشْرَبَانِ؟ عِنْدَنَا عَصِير وَمَاء وَمَشْرُوبَات بَارِدَة.
npc.en: And what will you two drink? We have juice, water and cold drinks.

choices.ar: زُجَاجَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْمَاء، لَوْ سَمَحْتَ. وَهَلِ الطَّعَام حَارّ؟
choices.en: Two bottles of water, please. And is the food spicy?
choices.feedback: Good: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ is another polite 'please' to a man, and asking about spice before the food comes is wise.

choices.ar: زُجَاجَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْمَاء، لَوْ سَمَحْتَ.
choices.en: Two bottles of water, please.
choices.feedback: Short and polite. زُجَاجَتَيْنِ ends in -ayni because it is what you order (an object).

choices.ar: زُجَاجَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْمَاء، لَوْ سَمَحْتِ.
choices.en: Two bottles of water, please (to a woman).
choices.feedback: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ (-ti) is for a woman. The waiter is a man: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ (-ta).

npc.ar: لَا، لَيْسَ حَارًّا. وَالصَّلْصَة الْحَارَّة عَلَى الطَّاوِلَة.
npc.en: No, it isn't spicy. And the hot sauce is on the table.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز، شُكْرًا لَكَ.
choices.en: Excellent, thank you.
choices.feedback: Good: شُكْرًا لَكَ thanks one man.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز، شُكْرًا لَكُمَا.
choices.en: Excellent, thank you both.
choices.feedback: لَكُمَا is for two people. You thank one waiter, a man: شُكْرًا لَكَ.

npc.ar: تَفَضَّلَا، الْمَحْشِيّ وَالسَّلَطَة. بِالْهَنَاء وَالشِّفَاء!
npc.en: Here you are, both of you: the stuffed vegetables and the salad. Enjoy your meal!
segs: please, here you are (to two people)

choices.ar: الْمَحْشِيّ لَذِيذ جِدًّا! الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: The stuffed vegetables are very delicious! The bill, please.
choices.feedback: Good: a compliment and then the bill. مَحْشِيّ is masculine, so لَذِيذ has no ة.

choices.ar: الْمَحْشِيّ لَذِيذَة جِدًّا! الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: The stuffed vegetables are very delicious! The bill, please (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: مَحْشِيّ is a masculine singular word, so the adjective has no ة: الْمَحْشِيّ لَذِيذ.

npc.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا آنِسَة! الْخُبْز طَازَج وَسَاخِن الْآن.
npc.en: Good morning, miss! The bread is fresh and hot right now.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور! أُرِيدُ خَمْسَةَ أَرْغِفَة مِنَ الْخُبْز الْبَلَدِيّ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Good morning! I'd like five loaves of country bread, please.
choices.feedback: Good: after the numbers three to ten the noun is plural: خَمْسَةَ أَرْغِفَة.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور! أُرِيدُ خَمْسَةَ رَغِيف مِنَ الْخُبْز الْبَلَدِيّ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Good morning! I'd like five loaf of country bread, please (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: After the numbers three to ten the noun is plural: خَمْسَةَ أَرْغِفَة, not خَمْسَةَ رَغِيف.

npc.ar: حَاضِر! هَلْ تُرِيدِينَ شَيْئًا آخَر؟ عِنْدَنَا كَعْك وَكَرْوَاسُون.
npc.en: Certainly! Would you like anything else? We have kaʿk biscuits and croissants.

choices.ar: بِكَمِ الْكَرْوَاسُون؟ وَبِكَمِ الْكَعْكَة؟
choices.en: How much is a croissant? And how much is one kaʿk?
choices.feedback: Good: بِكَمْ asks the price ('for how much?'), and before al- it becomes بِكَمِ.

choices.ar: لَا، شُكْرًا. هٰذَا كُلُّ شَيْء. كَمِ الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: No, thank you. That's everything. How much is the bill, please?
choices.feedback: Polite and complete: a 'no' with شُكْرًا, then you ask for the bill.

choices.ar: بِكَمِ الْكَرْوَاسُون، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ؟
choices.en: How much is a croissant, please (to a woman)?
choices.feedback: The baker says تُرِيدِينَ to you because you are a woman, but he is a man: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (-ka).

npc.ar: الْكَرْوَاسُون بِخَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ جُنَيْهًا، وَالْكَعْكَة بِعَشَرَةِ جُنَيْهَات.
npc.en: A croissant is fifteen pounds, and a kaʿk is ten pounds.

choices.ar: إِذًا أُرِيدُ قِطْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْكَرْوَاسُون، وَثَلَاثَ كَعْكَات.
choices.en: Then I'd like two croissants and three kaʿk biscuits.
choices.feedback: Good: the dual object ends in -ayni (قِطْعَتَيْنِ), and كَعْكَة is feminine, so 'three' has no ة: ثَلَاثَ كَعْكَات.

choices.ar: إِذًا أُرِيدُ قِطْعَتَانِ مِنَ الْكَرْوَاسُون، وَثَلَاثَ كَعْكَات.
choices.en: Then I'd like two croissants and three kaʿk biscuits (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: As the object of أُرِيدُ the dual ends in -ayni: أُرِيدُ قِطْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْكَرْوَاسُون.

npc.ar: تَفَضَّلِي: خَمْسَةُ أَرْغِفَة، وَقِطْعَتَانِ مِنَ الْكَرْوَاسُون، وَثَلَاثُ كَعْكَات.
npc.en: Here you are: five loaves, two croissants and three kaʿk biscuits.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا! كَمِ الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: Thank you! How much is the bill, please?
choices.feedback: Good: before al- the sukūn of كَمْ becomes i: كَمِ الْحِسَاب.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا! كَمْ حِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: Thank you! How much bill, please? (missing 'the')
choices.feedback: You ask about this bill, 'the bill', so use الـ: كَمِ الْحِسَاب؟

npc.ar: الْخُبْز بِعَشَرَة، وَالْكَرْوَاسُون بِثَلَاثِينَ، وَالْكَعْك بِثَلَاثِينَ. الْمَجْمُوع سَبْعُونَ جُنَيْهًا.
npc.en: The bread is ten, the croissants thirty and the kaʿk thirty. That's seventy pounds altogether.

choices.ar: تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذِهِ مِئَةُ جُنَيْه.
choices.en: Here you are, this is a hundred pounds.
choices.feedback: Good: after مِئَة the noun is singular (مِئَةُ جُنَيْه), and تَفَضَّلْ is 'here you are' to a man.

choices.ar: تَفَضَّلْ، سَبْعُونَ جُنَيْهًا.
choices.en: Here you are, seventy pounds.
choices.feedback: Good: the exact amount. After seventy the noun is singular with -an: جُنَيْهًا.

choices.ar: تَفَضَّلْ، سَبْعُونَ جُنَيْهَات.
choices.en: Here you are, seventy pounds (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: After 11 to 99 the noun is singular with the ending -an: سَبْعُونَ جُنَيْهًا.

npc.ar: الْخُبْز بِعَشَرَةِ جُنَيْهَات، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.
npc.en: The bread is ten pounds, please.

choices.ar: تَفَضَّلْ، عَشَرَةُ جُنَيْهَات. شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا!
choices.en: Here you are, ten pounds. Thank you very much!
choices.feedback: Good: after ten the noun is plural (جُنَيْهَات); from eleven on it becomes singular with -an.

choices.ar: تَفَضَّلِي، عَشَرَةُ جُنَيْهَات. شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا!
choices.en: Here you are (to a woman), ten pounds. Thank you very much!
choices.feedback: The baker says تَفَضَّلِي to you, a woman. To him, a man, say تَفَضَّلْ.

npc.ar: أَهْلًا يَا آنِسَة! كَيْفَ أُسَاعِدُكِ؟
npc.en: Hello, miss! How can I help you?

choices.ar: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ! أَيْنَ مَحَطَّةُ الْمِتْرُو، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: Excuse me! Where is the metro station, please?
choices.feedback: Good: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ (-ta) to a man, then أَيْنَ + the place.

choices.ar: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ! أَيْنَ مَحَطَّةُ الْمِتْرُو؟
choices.en: Excuse me (to a woman)! Where is the metro station?
choices.feedback: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ (-ti) is for a woman. The shopkeeper is a man: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ (-ta).

npc.ar: مَحَطَّةُ السَّادَات؟ هِيَ قَرِيبَة، فِي مَيْدَانِ التَّحْرِير.
npc.en: Sadat station? It is close, in Tahrir Square.
segs: Sadat (a metro station, named after an Egyptian president)

choices.ar: هَلْ هِيَ بَعِيدَة مَشْيًا؟ أَنَا لَا أَعْرِفُ هٰذِهِ الْمِنْطَقَة.
choices.en: Is it far on foot? I don't know this area.
choices.feedback: Good: مَحَطَّة is feminine, so 'it' is هِيَ and 'far' is بَعِيدَة.

choices.ar: هَلْ هِيَ بَعِيد مَشْيًا؟
choices.en: Is it far on foot? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: هِيَ (the station) is feminine, so the adjective takes ة: هَلْ هِيَ بَعِيدَة؟

npc.ar: لَا، عَشْرُ دَقَائِق فَقَطْ. اِذْهَبِي إِلَى الْأَمَام حَتَّى الْإِشَارَة.
npc.en: No, only ten minutes. Go straight ahead as far as the traffic lights.

choices.ar: حَتَّى الْإِشَارَة، ثُمَّ يَمِينًا أَمْ يَسَارًا؟
choices.en: As far as the traffic lights, and then right or left?
choices.feedback: Good: you repeat the key point to check it, and 'to the right / left' take -an: يَمِينًا، يَسَارًا.

choices.ar: حَتَّى الْإِشَارَة، ثُمَّ يَمِين أَمْ يَسَار؟
choices.en: As far as the traffic lights, and then right or left? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: يَمِين and يَسَار are the nouns 'right side, left side'. For a direction to go, add -an: يَمِينًا أَمْ يَسَارًا؟

npc.ar: ثُمَّ خُذِي الشَّارِعَ الثَّانِي عَلَى الْيَسَار.
npc.en: Then take the second street on the left.

choices.ar: الشَّارِع الثَّانِي عَلَى الْيَسَار. وَبَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ؟
choices.en: The second street on the left. And after that?
choices.feedback: Good: the ordinal comes after its noun, like any adjective: الشَّارِع الثَّانِي.

choices.ar: هَلْ هُنَاكَ عَلَامَة لِلْمِتْرُو؟
choices.en: Is there a sign for the metro?
choices.feedback: A smart question: a sign helps you find the station. هُنَاكَ means 'there is'.

choices.ar: الثَّانِي الشَّارِع عَلَى الْيَسَار. وَبَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ؟
choices.en: The second street on the left. And after that? (wrong word order)
choices.feedback: An ordinal comes after its noun, like any adjective: الشَّارِع الثَّانِي.

npc.ar: بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ تَرَيْنَ الْمَيْدَان. الْمَحَطَّة أَمَامَ الْمَتْحَف الْمِصْرِيّ تَقْرِيبًا.
npc.en: After that you will see the square. The station is more or less in front of the Egyptian Museum.

choices.ar: هَلْ هُنَاكَ عَلَامَة لِلْمِتْرُو؟
choices.en: Is there a sign for the metro?
choices.feedback: Good: هَلْ هُنَاكَ …؟ asks 'is there …?'.

choices.ar: هَلْ هُنَاكَ عَلَامَة لِلْمِتْرُو، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ؟
choices.en: Is there a sign for the metro, please (to a woman)?
choices.feedback: He uses -ī forms (تَرَيْنَ، خُذِي) because you are a woman, but he is a man: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (-ka).

npc.ar: نَعَم، هُنَاكَ عَلَامَة حَمْرَاء كَبِيرَة عَلَيْهَا حَرْف «م».
npc.en: Yes, there is a big red sign with the letter M on it.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! أَنْتَ لَطِيف جِدًّا.
choices.en: Thank you very much! You are very kind.
choices.feedback: Good: to a man, أَنْتَ لَطِيف, with no ة.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! أَنْتِ لَطِيفَة جِدًّا.
choices.en: Thank you very much! You are very kind (to a woman).
choices.feedback: أَنْتِ لَطِيفَة is said to a woman. The shopkeeper is a man: أَنْتَ لَطِيف.

npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! تَفَضَّلِي. هَلْ تَبْحَثِينَ عَنْ شَيْء خَاصّ؟
npc.en: Good evening! Come in. Are you looking for something special?

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ فُسْتَانًا لِحَفْلَةِ عِيدِ مِيلَاد.
choices.en: Good evening. I would like a dress for a birthday party.
choices.feedback: Good: فُسْتَانًا takes -an as the object of أُرِيدُ.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ فُسْتَان لِحَفْلَةِ عِيدِ مِيلَاد.
choices.en: Good evening. I would like a dress for a birthday party (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: The object of أُرِيدُ takes -an: أُرِيدُ فُسْتَانًا.

npc.ar: عِنْدَنَا فَسَاتِين جَدِيدَة كَثِيرَة. هٰذِهِ الْفَسَاتِين الْخَضْرَاء جَمِيلَة جِدًّا.
npc.en: We have lots of new dresses. These green dresses are very pretty.

choices.ar: نَعَم، هِيَ جَمِيلَة. هَلْ عِنْدَكَ هٰذَا الْفُسْتَان بِمَقَاس صَغِير؟
choices.en: Yes, they are pretty. Do you have this dress in a small size?
choices.feedback: Good: plurals of things take هِيَ and a feminine singular adjective, but one dress is masculine: هٰذَا الْفُسْتَان.

choices.ar: نَعَم، هِيَ جَمِيلَة. هَلْ عِنْدَكَ هٰذَا الْفُسْتَان بِمَقَاس مُتَوَسِّط؟
choices.en: Yes, they are pretty. Do you have this dress in a medium size?
choices.feedback: Good: مَقَاس is masculine, so 'medium' has no ة: بِمَقَاس مُتَوَسِّط.

choices.ar: نَعَم، هٰذِهِ الْفَسَاتِين جَمِيلُونَ.
choices.en: Yes, these dresses are pretty (wrong ending).
choices.feedback: -ūna is for groups of people. Plurals of things take a feminine singular adjective: هٰذِهِ الْفَسَاتِين جَمِيلَة.

npc.ar: طَبْعًا، تَفَضَّلِي. غُرْفَةُ الْقِيَاس هُنَاكَ، عَلَى الْيَمِين.
npc.en: Of course, here you are. The fitting room is over there, on the right.

choices.ar: لِلْأَسَف، الْفُسْتَان ضَيِّق قَلِيلًا. هَلْ هُنَاكَ مَقَاس أَكْبَر؟
choices.en: Unfortunately, the dress is a little tight. Is there a bigger size?
choices.feedback: Good: فُسْتَان is masculine, even though women wear it, so ضَيِّق has no ة.

choices.ar: لِلْأَسَف، الْفُسْتَان ضَيِّقَة قَلِيلًا. هَلْ هُنَاكَ مَقَاس أَكْبَر؟
choices.en: Unfortunately, the dress is a little tight. Is there a bigger size? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: فُسْتَان (dress) is masculine, even though women wear it: الْفُسْتَان ضَيِّق.

npc.ar: نَعَم، هٰذَا الْمَقَاس الْمُتَوَسِّط. هُوَ مُنَاسِب لَكِ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه.
npc.en: Yes, this is the medium size. It should be right for you, God willing.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز! هٰذَا الْمَقَاس جَيِّد: لَا ضَيِّق وَلَا وَاسِع. بِكَمْ هُوَ؟
choices.en: Excellent! This size is good: neither tight nor loose. How much is it?
choices.feedback: Good: لَا … وَلَا … is 'neither … nor …', and بِكَمْ هُوَ؟ asks the price of it.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز! هٰذَا الْمَقَاس جَيِّد. بِكَمْ هِيَ؟
choices.en: Excellent! This size is good. How much is it? (wrong pronoun)
choices.feedback: You ask about one dress (فُسْتَان, masculine), so 'it' is هُوَ: بِكَمْ هُوَ؟

npc.ar: بِسَبْعِمِئَة جُنَيْه. وَعِنْدَنَا أَيْضًا أَحْذِيَة مُنَاسِبَة لِلْفُسْتَان.
npc.en: Seven hundred pounds. And we also have shoes that go with the dress.

choices.ar: لَا، شُكْرًا. عِنْدِي أَحْذِيَة كَثِيرَة فِي الْبَيْت!
choices.en: No, thank you. I have lots of shoes at home!
choices.feedback: Polite and clear. أَحْذِيَة is a plural of things, so 'many' is feminine singular: كَثِيرَة.

choices.ar: لَا، شُكْرًا. عِنْدِي أَحْذِيَة كَثِيرُونَ فِي الْبَيْت!
choices.en: No, thank you. I have lots of shoes at home! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: Shoes are things, not people, so the adjective is feminine singular: أَحْذِيَة كَثِيرَة.

npc.ar: كَمَا تُحِبِّينَ. تَفَضَّلِي، الْفُسْتَان فِي الْحَقِيبَة. مَبْرُوك!
npc.en: As you like. Here you are, the dress is in the bag. Congratulations!

choices.ar: اللّٰه يُبَارِكُ فِيكَ! شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.
choices.en: God bless you! Thank you very much.
choices.feedback: Good: اللّٰه يُبَارِكُ فِيكَ is the usual answer to مَبْرُوك, with -ka to a man.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much! Goodbye.
choices.feedback: Fine too: a warm thank-you and goodbye.

choices.ar: اللّٰه يُبَارِكُ فِيكِ! شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.
choices.en: God bless you (to a woman)! Thank you very much.
choices.feedback: فِيكِ (-ki) is for a woman. The shop assistant is a man: اللّٰه يُبَارِكُ فِيكَ.

npc.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا! أَنْتَ فَيْصَل؟ تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذِهِ هِيَ الشَّقَّة.
npc.en: Welcome! Are you Faisal? Please come in, this is the flat.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا أُسْتَاذ مَحْمُود. هَلِ الشَّقَّة مَفْرُوشَة؟
choices.en: Thank you, Mr Mahmoud. Is the flat furnished?
choices.feedback: Good: شَقَّة is feminine, so 'furnished' takes ة: مَفْرُوشَة.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا أُسْتَاذ مَحْمُود. هَلِ الشَّقَّة مَفْرُوش؟
choices.en: Thank you, Mr Mahmoud. Is the flat furnished? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: شَقَّة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة: هَلِ الشَّقَّة مَفْرُوشَة؟

npc.ar: نَعَم، فِيهَا سَرِير وَمَكْتَب وَخِزَانَة، وَفِي غُرْفَةِ الْجُلُوس كَنَبَة.
npc.en: Yes, there is a bed, a desk and a wardrobe, and there is a sofa in the living room.

choices.ar: وَالْمَطْبَخ؟ هَلْ فِيهِ ثَلَّاجَة؟
choices.en: And the kitchen? Is there a fridge in it?
choices.feedback: Good: مَطْبَخ is masculine, so 'in it' is فِيهِ, and 'a fridge' has no الـ.

choices.ar: وَالْحَمَّام؟ هَلْ فِيهِ مَاء سَاخِن؟
choices.en: And the bathroom? Is there hot water?
choices.feedback: Good: مَاء is masculine, so سَاخِن has no ة.

choices.ar: وَالْمَطْبَخ؟ هَلْ فِيهِ الثَّلَّاجَة؟
choices.en: And the kitchen? Is the fridge in it? (wrong 'the')
choices.feedback: To ask 'is there a …?', the thing has no الـ: هَلْ فِيهِ ثَلَّاجَة؟

npc.ar: الْمَطْبَخ صَغِير، وَلَيْسَ فِيهِ ثَلَّاجَة، لٰكِنْ فِيهِ فُرْن جَدِيد.
npc.en: The kitchen is small, and there is no fridge, but there is a new oven.

choices.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة. وَالْحَمَّام؟ هَلْ فِيهِ مَاء سَاخِن؟
choices.en: No problem. And the bathroom? Is there hot water?
choices.feedback: Good: لَا مُشْكِلَة keeps it friendly, and مَاء is masculine, so سَاخِن has no ة.

choices.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة. وَالْحَمَّام؟ هَلْ فِيهِ مَاء سَاخِنَة؟
choices.en: No problem. And the bathroom? Is there hot water? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: مَاء is masculine, so the adjective has no ة: مَاء سَاخِن.

npc.ar: طَبْعًا! وَهٰذِهِ الشُّرْفَة. اُنْظُرْ، مِنْ هُنَا تَرَى النِّيل.
npc.en: Of course! And this is the balcony. Look, from here you can see the Nile.

choices.ar: جَمِيل جِدًّا! كَمِ الْإِيجَار فِي الشَّهْر، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: Very beautiful! How much is the rent per month, please?
choices.feedback: Good: كَمِ الْإِيجَار, with الـ, and the m of كَمْ takes an i to link to it.

choices.ar: جَمِيل جِدًّا! كَمْ إِيجَار فِي الشَّهْر؟
choices.en: Very beautiful! How much rent per month? (missing 'the')
choices.feedback: You ask about 'the rent' of this flat, so use الـ: كَمِ الْإِيجَار؟

npc.ar: سَبْعَةُ آلَافِ جُنَيْه فِي الشَّهْر، وَالتَّأْمِين شَهْر وَاحِد.
npc.en: Seven thousand pounds a month, and the deposit is one month's rent.

choices.ar: هٰذَا مُنَاسِب. هَلِ الْكَهْرَبَاء وَالْمَاء مَعَ الْإِيجَار؟
choices.en: That's fine. Are electricity and water included in the rent?
choices.feedback: Good: هٰذَا is masculine, so مُنَاسِب has no ة. Asking about the bills before you agree is wise.

choices.ar: هٰذَا مُنَاسِبَة. هَلِ الْكَهْرَبَاء وَالْمَاء مَعَ الْإِيجَار؟
choices.en: That's fine. Are electricity and water included in the rent? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: هٰذَا is masculine, so the adjective has no ة: هٰذَا مُنَاسِب.

npc.ar: لَا، الْكَهْرَبَاء عَلَيْكَ، وَالْمَاء عَلَيَّ.
npc.en: No, you pay for the electricity, and I pay for the water.
segs: on you: your cost (to a man)

choices.ar: اِتَّفَقْنَا! شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا أُسْتَاذ مَحْمُود.
choices.en: It's a deal! Thank you very much, Mr Mahmoud.
choices.feedback: Good: اِتَّفَقْنَا (lit. 'we have agreed') closes a deal.

choices.ar: طَيِّب، الْكَهْرَبَاء عَلَيْكَ. اِتَّفَقْنَا!
choices.en: OK, you pay for the electricity. It's a deal! (wrong pronoun)
segs: on you: your cost (to a man)
choices.feedback: You copied his words, but from your side the pronoun swaps: he said الْكَهْرَبَاء عَلَيْكَ (on you), so you say الْكَهْرَبَاء عَلَيَّ (on me, my cost).

npc.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا يَا فَيْصَل! تَفَضَّلْ، الْبَيْت بَيْتُكَ.
npc.en: Welcome, Faisal! Please come in and make yourself at home.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا أُسْتَاذ أَحْمَد. هٰذِهِ حَلَوِيَّات لَكُمْ.
choices.en: Thank you, Mr Ahmad. These sweets are for you.
choices.feedback: Good: a small gift of sweets is the custom, and لَكُمْ (for you, plural) gives it to the whole family.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا أُسْتَاذ أَحْمَد. هٰذَا حَلَوِيَّات لَكُمْ.
choices.en: Thank you, Mr Ahmad. These sweets are for you (wrong form of 'this').
choices.feedback: حَلَوِيَّات is a plural of things, and such plurals take feminine singular words: هٰذِهِ حَلَوِيَّات، not هٰذَا.

npc.ar: أَهْلًا يَا فَيْصَل! مَاذَا تَشْرَبُ؟ عِنْدَنَا شَاي وَقَهْوَة وَعَصِير.
npc.en: Hello, Faisal! What would you like to drink? We have tea, coffee and juice.

choices.ar: شَاي، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ، بِدُونِ سُكَّر. بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيل جِدًّا!
choices.en: Tea, please, without sugar. Your home is very beautiful!
choices.feedback: Good: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ (-ki) to Dr Fatima, and بَيْتُكُمْ (-kum) because the home belongs to the whole family.

choices.ar: قَهْوَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ، بِدُونِ سُكَّر. بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيل جِدًّا!
choices.en: Coffee, please, without sugar. Your home is very beautiful!
choices.feedback: Good: coffee instead of tea, with -ki to Dr Fatima and a compliment for the home.

choices.ar: شَاي، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، بِدُونِ سُكَّر. بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيل جِدًّا!
choices.en: Tea, please, without sugar. Your home is very beautiful! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (-ka) is for a man. Dr Fatima is a woman: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ (-ki).

npc.ar: تَفَضَّلِ الشَّاي، وَخُذْ قِطْعَةَ كَعْك أُخْرَى!
npc.en: Here's your tea, and have another piece of cake!

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا، الْكَعْك لَذِيذ، لٰكِنْ يَكْفِي، أَنَا شَبْعَان!
choices.en: Thank you so much, the cake is delicious, but that's enough, I'm full!
choices.feedback: Polite and clear: praise the food first, then يَكْفِي (that's enough) when you are really full.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا، الْكَعْك لَذِيذَة، لٰكِنْ يَكْفِي، أَنَا شَبْعَان!
choices.en: Thank you so much, the cake is delicious, but that's enough, I'm full! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: كَعْك is masculine, so the adjective has no ة: الْكَعْك لَذِيذ.

npc.ar: تَفَضَّلِ الْقَهْوَة، وَخُذْ قِطْعَةَ كَعْك أُخْرَى!
npc.en: Here's your coffee, and have another piece of cake!

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا، الْكَعْك لَذِيذ، لٰكِنْ يَكْفِي، أَنَا شَبْعَان!
choices.en: Thank you so much, the cake is delicious, but that's enough, I'm full!
choices.feedback: Polite and clear: praise the food first, then يَكْفِي (that's enough) when you are really full.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا، الْكَعْك لَذِيذ، لٰكِنْ يَكْفِي، أَنَا شَبْعَانَة!
choices.en: Thank you so much, the cake is delicious, but that's enough, I'm full! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: شَبْعَانَة is the feminine, said by a woman. You are a man: أَنَا شَبْعَان.

npc.ar: لَا، لَا! أَنْتَ نَحِيف جِدًّا. كُلْ، كُلْ!
npc.en: No, no! You're far too thin. Eat, eat!

choices.ar: حَاضِر يَا دُكْتُورَة! قِطْعَة صَغِيرَة فَقَطْ، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.
choices.en: All right, doctor! Just a small piece, please.
choices.feedback: Good: accepting a little is polite. قِطْعَة is feminine, so 'small' is صَغِيرَة.

choices.ar: حَاضِر يَا دُكْتُورَة! قِطْعَة صَغِير فَقَطْ، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.
choices.en: All right, doctor! Just a small piece, please. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: قِطْعَة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة too: قِطْعَة صَغِيرَة.

npc.ar: يَا فَيْصَل، بَيْتُنَا مَفْتُوح لَكَ دَائِمًا. أَنْتَ مِنَ الْعَائِلَة الْآن.
npc.en: Faisal, our home is always open to you. You're one of the family now.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا لَكُمْ، أَنْتُمْ عَائِلَة كَرِيمَة جِدًّا.
choices.en: Thank you all, you are a very generous family.
choices.feedback: Good: لَكُمْ and أَنْتُمْ thank the whole family, and كَرِيمَة agrees with عَائِلَة (feminine).

choices.ar: شُكْرًا لَكُمْ، أَنْتَ عَائِلَة كَرِيمَة جِدًّا.
choices.en: Thank you all, you (one man) are a very generous family. (wrong word)
choices.feedback: A family is several people, so 'you' is plural: أَنْتُمْ عَائِلَة كَرِيمَة جِدًّا.

npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر، مَكْتَبُ الْمَفْقُودَات. كَيْفَ أُسَاعِدُكَ؟
npc.en: Good evening, lost property office. How can I help you?

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. نَسِيتُ حَقِيبَتِي فِي قِطَارِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة، وَلَمْ أَجِدْهَا.
choices.en: Good evening. I left my bag on the train from Alexandria, and I couldn't find it.
choices.feedback: Good: after لَمْ the verb loses its final -u, so lam ajid-hā (أَجِدْهَا).

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. نَسِيتُ حَقِيبَتِي فِي قِطَارِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة، وَلَمْ أَجِدُهَا.
choices.en: Good evening. I left my bag on the train from Alexandria, and I couldn't find it. (wrong ending)
segs: I find it (f; ordinary present form)
choices.feedback: After لَمْ the verb loses its final -u: لَمْ أَجِدْهَا (lam ajid-hā), not lam ajidu-hā.

npc.ar: مَتَى وَصَلَ الْقِطَار؟ وَفِي أَيِّ عَرَبَة جَلَسْتَ؟
npc.en: When did the train arrive? And which carriage did you sit in?

choices.ar: وَصَلَ فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة مَسَاءً. جَلَسْتُ فِي الْعَرَبَة رَقْم أَرْبَعَة.
choices.en: It arrived at nine in the evening. I sat in carriage number four.
choices.feedback: Good: you answer both questions, and her جَلَسْتَ (you sat) becomes your جَلَسْتُ (I sat).

choices.ar: وَصَلَ فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة مَسَاءً. جَلَسْتَ فِي الْعَرَبَة رَقْم أَرْبَعَة.
choices.en: It arrived at nine in the evening. You sat in carriage number four. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: جَلَسْتَ (-ta) means 'you sat'. For 'I sat' the ending is -tu: جَلَسْتُ.

npc.ar: وَلِمَاذَا لَمْ تَأْخُذِ الْحَقِيبَة مَعَكَ؟ هَلْ نِمْتَ فِي الْقِطَار؟
npc.en: And why didn't you take the bag with you? Did you fall asleep on the train?

choices.ar: نَعَم، نِمْتُ قَلِيلًا، وَبَعْدَ أَنْ وَصَلْنَا خَرَجْتُ بِسُرْعَة مَعَ صَدِيقِي.
choices.en: Yes, I slept a little, and after we arrived I got off in a hurry with my friend.
segs: I went out, I got off
choices.feedback: Good: نَعَم answers 'did you fall asleep?', and the rest explains why you forgot the bag.

choices.ar: لَا، نِمْتُ قَلِيلًا.
choices.en: No, I slept a little.
choices.feedback: لَا (no) and then 'I slept' contradict each other. You did fall asleep: نَعَم، نِمْتُ قَلِيلًا.

npc.ar: مَا لَوْنُ الْحَقِيبَة؟ وَمَاذَا كَانَ فِيهَا؟
npc.en: What colour is the bag? And what was in it?

choices.ar: هِيَ حَقِيبَة زَرْقَاء صَغِيرَة. كَانَ فِيهَا كِتَاب وَكَامِيرَا وَمِفْتَاحُ شَقَّتِي.
choices.en: It's a small blue bag. There was a book in it, a camera and the key to my flat.
choices.feedback: Good: both answers at once. حَقِيبَة is feminine, so the colour is زَرْقَاء and 'small' is صَغِيرَة.

choices.ar: هِيَ حَقِيبَة زَرْقَاء صَغِيرَة.
choices.en: It's a small blue bag.
choices.feedback: Good: the colour first, in the feminine زَرْقَاء to agree with حَقِيبَة. She will ask about the contents next.

choices.ar: هِيَ حَقِيبَة أَزْرَق صَغِيرَة.
choices.en: It's a small blue bag. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: أَزْرَق is the masculine. حَقِيبَة is feminine, so the colour is feminine too: حَقِيبَة زَرْقَاء.

npc.ar: وَمَاذَا كَانَ فِيهَا؟
npc.en: And what was in it?

choices.ar: كَانَ فِيهَا كِتَاب وَكَامِيرَا وَمِفْتَاحُ شَقَّتِي.
choices.en: There was a book in it, a camera and the key to my flat.
choices.feedback: Good: كَانَ فِيهَا (there was in it) uses her own words, with -hā for the bag.

choices.ar: كَانَ فِيهِ كِتَاب وَكَامِيرَا وَمِفْتَاحُ شَقَّتِي.
choices.en: There was a book in it, a camera and the key to my flat. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: فِيهِ (-hi) points to a masculine word. The bag, حَقِيبَة, is feminine: كَانَ فِيهَا.

npc.ar: أَنْتَ مَحْظُوظ! وَجَدُوا حَقِيبَة زَرْقَاء فِي الْعَرَبَة رَقْم أَرْبَعَة. هَلْ هٰذِهِ حَقِيبَتُكَ؟
npc.en: You're lucky! They found a blue bag in carriage number four. Is this your bag?

choices.ar: نَعَم، هٰذِهِ هِيَ! الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه! شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.
choices.en: Yes, that's the one! Thank God! Thank you very much.
choices.feedback: Good: هٰذِهِ هِيَ (this is it) is feminine because it stands for حَقِيبَة.

choices.ar: نَعَم، هٰذَا هُوَ! الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه! شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.
choices.en: Yes, that's the one! Thank God! Thank you very much. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: هٰذَا هُوَ is masculine, but you mean the bag, حَقِيبَة, which is feminine: هٰذِهِ هِيَ.

choices.ar: نَعَم، هٰذِهِ هِيَ! شُكْرًا لَكَ.
choices.en: Yes, that's the one! Thank you. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: لَكَ (-ka) is for a man. The clerk is a woman: شُكْرًا لَكِ (-ki), or simply شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.

npc.ar: أَهْلًا يَا فَيْصَل! كَيْفَ كَانَتْ عُطْلَتُكَ؟ أَيْنَ ذَهَبْتَ؟
npc.en: Hi, Faisal! How was your holiday? Where did you go?

choices.ar: كَانَتْ رَائِعَةً! سَافَرْتُ مَعَ صَدِيقِي إِلَى الْأُقْصُر وَأَسْوَان.
choices.en: It was wonderful! I travelled to Luxor and Aswan with my friend.
choices.feedback: Good: عُطْلَة is feminine, so كَانَتْ رَائِعَةً, with -an after 'was'.

choices.ar: كَانَ رَائِعًا! سَافَرْتُ مَعَ صَدِيقِي إِلَى الْأُقْصُر وَأَسْوَان.
choices.en: It was wonderful! I travelled to Luxor and Aswan with my friend. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: 'It' is the holiday, عُطْلَة, which is feminine: كَانَتْ رَائِعَةً.

npc.ar: وَمَاذَا فَعَلْتُمَا فِي الْأُقْصُر؟
npc.en: And what did you two do in Luxor?

choices.ar: زُرْنَا الْمَعَابِد الْقَدِيمَة، وَفِي الصَّبَاح الْبَاكِر رَكِبْنَا مُنْطَادًا فَوْقَ النِّيل.
choices.en: We visited the ancient temples, and early in the morning we went up in a balloon over the Nile.
choices.feedback: Good: she asks 'you two' (-tumā), and you answer with 'we' (-nā): زُرْنَا، رَكِبْنَا.

choices.ar: زُرْتُمَا الْمَعَابِد الْقَدِيمَة.
choices.en: You two visited the ancient temples. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: زُرْتُمَا means 'you two visited'. You and your friend are 'we': زُرْنَا الْمَعَابِد الْقَدِيمَة.

npc.ar: يَا سَلَام! وَهَلْ كَانَ الْجَوُّ حَارًّا هُنَاكَ؟
npc.en: Wow! And was the weather hot there?

choices.ar: كَانَ حَارًّا فِي النَّهَار، لٰكِنَّهُ كَانَ لَطِيفًا فِي الْمَسَاء. وَأَنْتِ؟ لَمْ تَذْهَبِي إِلَى أَيِّ مَكَان؟
choices.en: It was hot in the daytime, but it was pleasant in the evening. And you? Didn't you go anywhere?
segs: you go (to a woman; form after 'lam')
choices.feedback: Good: after لَمْ, تَذْهَبِينَ loses its -na: لَمْ تَذْهَبِي. And you turn the question back to Maryam.

choices.ar: كَانَ حَارًّا فِي النَّهَار، لٰكِنَّهُ كَانَ لَطِيفًا فِي الْمَسَاء. وَأَنْتِ يَا مَرْيَم؟ أَيْنَ ذَهَبْتِ؟
choices.en: It was hot in the daytime, but it was pleasant in the evening. And you, Maryam? Where did you go?
choices.feedback: Good: الْجَوّ is masculine (كَانَ حَارًّا), and ذَهَبْتِ (-ti) asks a woman where she went.

choices.ar: كَانَ الْجَوُّ حَارَّةً فِي النَّهَار.
choices.en: The weather was hot in the daytime. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: الْجَوّ (the weather) is masculine, so the adjective has no ة: كَانَ الْجَوُّ حَارًّا فِي النَّهَار.

npc.ar: لَا، لَمْ أُسَافِرْ. زَارَنَا أَقَارِبِي مِنَ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة، وَهُمْ بَقُوا عِنْدَنَا أُسْبُوعًا كَامِلًا.
npc.en: No, I didn't travel. My relatives from Alexandria visited us, and they stayed with us for a whole week.

choices.ar: وَهَلْ خَرَجْتُمْ مَعًا يَا مَرْيَم؟
choices.en: And did you all go out together, Maryam?
choices.feedback: Good: Maryam and her relatives are several people, so 'you went out' is خَرَجْتُمْ (-tum).

choices.ar: وَهَلْ خَرَجْتِ مَعًا يَا مَرْيَم؟
choices.en: And did you (one woman) go out together, Maryam? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: مَعًا (together) needs more than one person. You mean Maryam and her relatives: خَرَجْتُمْ مَعًا.

npc.ar: لَمْ أُسَافِرْ. زَارَنَا أَقَارِبِي مِنَ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة، وَهُمْ بَقُوا عِنْدَنَا أُسْبُوعًا كَامِلًا.
npc.en: I didn't travel. My relatives from Alexandria visited us, and they stayed with us for a whole week.

choices.ar: وَهَلْ خَرَجْتُمْ مَعًا يَا مَرْيَم؟
choices.en: And did you all go out together, Maryam?
choices.feedback: Good: Maryam and her relatives are several people, so 'you went out' is خَرَجْتُمْ (-tum).

choices.ar: وَهَلْ خَرَجْتَ مَعَهُمْ يَا مَرْيَم؟
choices.en: And did you go out with them, Maryam? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: خَرَجْتَ (-ta) is for a man. To Maryam say خَرَجْتِ (-ti), or ask about them all: وَهَلْ خَرَجْتُمْ مَعًا؟

npc.ar: نَعَم، ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْأَهْرَام. لٰكِنْ أَخِي لَمْ يَذْهَبْ مَعَنَا، لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ مَرِيضًا.
npc.en: Yes, we went to the pyramids. But my brother didn't come with us, because he was ill.

choices.ar: سَلَامَتُهُ! أَرْجُو أَنْ يَكُونَ بِخَيْر الْآنَ.
choices.en: I'm sorry he was ill! I hope he is well now.
choices.feedback: Good: سَلَامَتُهُ is the polite wish for someone who is ill, with -hu for her brother.

choices.ar: سَلَامَتُهَا! أَرْجُو أَنْ تَكُونَ بِخَيْر الْآنَ.
choices.en: May she get well! I hope she is well now. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: Her brother was ill, so use 'he' forms: سَلَامَتُهُ! أَرْجُو أَنْ يَكُونَ بِخَيْر الْآنَ.

npc.ar: تَفَضَّلِي، اِجْلِسِي هُنَا. مِمَّ تَشْكِينَ؟
npc.en: Please come in and sit here. What seems to be the problem?

choices.ar: يُؤْلِمُنِي حَلْقِي كَثِيرًا، وَعِنْدِي حَرَارَة مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْنِ.
choices.en: My throat hurts a lot, and I have had a temperature for two days.
choices.feedback: Good: حَلْق (throat) is masculine, so the verb starts with yu-: يُؤْلِمُنِي حَلْقِي.

choices.ar: تُؤْلِمُنِي حَلْقِي كَثِيرًا، وَعِنْدِي حَرَارَة مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْنِ.
choices.en: My throat hurts a lot, and I have had a temperature for two days. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: حَلْق (throat) is masculine, so the verb starts with yu-, not tu-: يُؤْلِمُنِي حَلْقِي.

npc.ar: هَلْ عِنْدَكِ سُعَال أَوْ صُدَاع أَيْضًا؟
npc.en: Do you also have a cough or a headache?

choices.ar: عِنْدِي صُدَاع فِي الْمَسَاء، لٰكِنْ لَيْسَ عِنْدِي سُعَال.
choices.en: I have a headache in the evening, but I don't have a cough.
choices.feedback: Good: his عِنْدَكِ (you have) becomes your عِنْدِي (I have), and لَيْسَ عِنْدِي says what you don't have.

choices.ar: عِنْدَكِ صُدَاع فِي الْمَسَاء، لٰكِنْ لَيْسَ عِنْدَكِ سُعَال.
choices.en: You have a headache in the evening, but you don't have a cough. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: عِنْدَكِ means 'you have'; you copied the question. About yourself say عِنْدِي: عِنْدِي صُدَاع … لَيْسَ عِنْدِي سُعَال.

npc.ar: طَيِّب. اِفْتَحِي فَمَكِ، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ… حَلْقُكِ أَحْمَر جِدًّا.
npc.en: OK. Open your mouth, please… Your throat is very red.

choices.ar: هَلْ هٰذَا خَطِير يَا دُكْتُور؟
choices.en: Is it serious, doctor?
choices.feedback: Good: هَلْ starts a yes/no question, and يَا دُكْتُور is the usual way to address a doctor.

choices.ar: هَلْ يَجِبُ أَنْ آخُذَ دَوَاءً؟
choices.en: Do I have to take any medicine?
choices.feedback: Good: after أَنْ the verb ends in -a (آخُذَ), and دَوَاءً takes -an as the object.

choices.ar: هَلْ هٰذَا خَطِيرَة يَا دُكْتُور؟
choices.en: Is it serious, doctor? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: هٰذَا is masculine, so the adjective has no ة: هَلْ هٰذَا خَطِير؟

npc.ar: لَا، لَا تَقْلَقِي. حَلْقُكِ مُلْتَهِب فَقَطْ، وَهٰذَا لَيْسَ خَطِيرًا.
npc.en: No, don't worry. Your throat is just inflamed, and that isn't serious.

choices.ar: هَلْ يَجِبُ أَنْ آخُذَ دَوَاءً؟
choices.en: Do I have to take any medicine?
choices.feedback: Good: after أَنْ the verb ends in -a (آخُذَ), and دَوَاءً takes -an as the object.

choices.ar: هَلْ يَجِبُ أَنْ آخُذُ دَوَاءً؟
choices.en: Do I have to take any medicine? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: After أَنْ the verb ends in -a, not -u: أَنْ آخُذَ.

npc.ar: نَعَم، هٰذِهِ وَصْفَة: حَبَّة مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم، خَمْسَةَ أَيَّام.
npc.en: Yes, here is a prescription: one tablet twice a day for five days.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا دُكْتُور. حَبَّة مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم، خَمْسَةَ أَيَّام.
choices.en: Thank you, doctor. One tablet twice a day, for five days.
choices.feedback: Good: repeating the dose back is a sensible way to check you understood it.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا دُكْتُورَة. حَبَّة مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم، خَمْسَةَ أَيَّام.
choices.en: Thank you, doctor (to a woman). One tablet twice a day, for five days. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: دُكْتُورَة is a woman doctor. This doctor is a man: يَا دُكْتُور.

npc.ar: وَلَا تَشْرَبِي مَشْرُوبَات بَارِدَة، وَارْتَاحِي فِي الْبَيْت.
npc.en: And don't drink cold drinks, and rest at home.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا دُكْتُور، مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much, doctor. Goodbye.
choices.feedback: Good: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا and مَعَ السَّلَامَة close the visit politely.

choices.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا يَا دُكْتُور.
choices.en: Welcome, doctor.
choices.feedback: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا greets someone who arrives. You are leaving, so thank him and say goodbye: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا دُكْتُور، مَعَ السَّلَامَة.

npc.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر! كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكَ؟
npc.en: Good morning! How can I help you?

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ دَوَاءً لِلسُّعَال لِأُخْتِي الصَّغِيرَة.
choices.en: Good morning. I want to buy some cough medicine for my little sister.
choices.feedback: Good: أَنْ joins the two verbs, and the second one ends in -a: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ أَشْتَرِي دَوَاءً لِلسُّعَال لِأُخْتِي الصَّغِيرَة.
choices.en: Good morning. I want to buy some cough medicine for my little sister. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: Join the two verbs with أَنْ, and the second verb ends in -a: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ دَوَاءً.

npc.ar: كَمْ عُمْرُهَا؟ وَهَلْ عِنْدَهَا حَرَارَة؟
npc.en: How old is she? And does she have a temperature?

choices.ar: عُمْرُهَا سِتّ سَنَوَات، وَلَيْسَ عِنْدَهَا حَرَارَة، الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه.
choices.en: She is six years old, and she doesn't have a temperature, thank God.
choices.feedback: Good: -hā (her) all through, and سِتّ has no ة because سَنَة (year) is feminine.

choices.ar: عُمْرُهُ سِتّ سَنَوَات، وَلَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ حَرَارَة، الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه.
choices.en: He is six years old, and he doesn't have a temperature, thank God. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: -hu means 'his'. You are talking about your sister: عُمْرُهَا … عِنْدَهَا (-hā).

npc.ar: إِذًا هٰذَا الشَّرَاب جَيِّد لِلْأَطْفَال، وَهُوَ بِطَعْمِ الْفَرَاوِلَة.
npc.en: Then this syrup is good for children, and it tastes of strawberry.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز! نُور تُحِبُّ الْفَرَاوِلَة. كَمْ مَرَّةً فِي الْيَوْم؟
choices.en: Excellent! Nour loves strawberries. How many times a day?
choices.feedback: Good: تُحِبُّ (ta-) for Nour, a girl, and after كَمْ the noun is singular with -an: كَمْ مَرَّةً.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز! نُور يُحِبُّ الْفَرَاوِلَة. كَمْ مَرَّةً فِي الْيَوْم؟
choices.en: Excellent! Nour loves strawberries. How many times a day? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: يُحِبُّ (yu-) is 'he loves'. Nour is a girl: نُور تُحِبُّ (tu-).

npc.ar: مِلْعَقَة صَغِيرَة ثَلَاثَ مَرَّات فِي الْيَوْم، بَعْدَ الْأَكْل.
npc.en: One small spoonful three times a day, after food.

choices.ar: فَهِمْتُ. وَهَلْ تَبِيعُونَ مَنَادِيل وَعَسَلًا أَيْضًا؟
choices.en: I see. And do you sell tissues and honey too?
choices.feedback: Good: تَبِيعُونَ (you sell, plural) asks about the whole pharmacy, not one person.

choices.ar: فَهِمْتُ. كَمِ الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: I see. How much is that, please?
choices.feedback: Good: before al- the sukūn of كَمْ becomes i, كَمِ الْحِسَاب, and -ka is right for the pharmacist.

choices.ar: فَهِمْتُ. كَمِ الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ؟
choices.en: I see. How much is that, please? (to a woman)
choices.feedback: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ (-ki) is for a woman. The pharmacist is a man: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (-ka).

npc.ar: الْمَنَادِيل هُنَاكَ، لٰكِنْ لَيْسَ عِنْدَنَا عَسَل، آسِف.
npc.en: The tissues are over there, but we don't have any honey, sorry.

choices.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة. كَمِ الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: No problem. How much is that, please?
choices.feedback: Good: لَا مُشْكِلَة answers his 'sorry', then you ask for the bill politely.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا، اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ.
choices.en: Thanks, God keep you safe.
choices.feedback: اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ answers a get-well wish like سَلَامَتُهَا. Here he says sorry, so answer لَا مُشْكِلَة.

npc.ar: خَمْسَة وَأَرْبَعُونَ جُنَيْهًا. سَلَامَتُهَا!
npc.en: Forty-five pounds. I hope she gets well soon!
segs: (wishing) her safety: 'get well soon' (about a woman)

choices.ar: شُكْرًا، اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ. مَعَ السَّلَامَة!
choices.en: Thanks, God keep you safe. Goodbye!
choices.feedback: Good: اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ is the set answer to سَلَامَتُهَا, with -ka for the pharmacist.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا، اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكِ. مَعَ السَّلَامَة!
choices.en: Thanks, God keep you safe (to a woman). Goodbye! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: يُسَلِّمُكِ (-ki) is for a woman. The pharmacist is a man: اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ (-ka).

npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر يَا فَيْصَل! أَنَا جَارَتُكَ سُعَاد، مِنَ الطَّابِق الثَّالِث.
npc.en: Good evening, Faisal! I'm your neighbour Suad, from the third floor.
segs: your neighbour (a woman; to a man)

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور يَا سَيِّدَة سُعَاد! تَفَضَّلِي، كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكِ؟
choices.en: Good evening, Mrs Suad! Please come in. How can I help you?
segs: I help you (to a woman, after an)
choices.feedback: Good: تَفَضَّلِي and أُسَاعِدَكِ both end in the -i of a woman.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور يَا سَيِّدَة سُعَاد! تَفَضَّلْ، كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكِ؟
choices.en: Good evening, Mrs Suad! Please come in (to a man). How can I help you? (wrong ending)
segs: I help you (to a woman, after an)
choices.feedback: تَفَضَّلْ is said to a man. To Mrs Suad say تَفَضَّلِي.

npc.ar: شُكْرًا، لَنْ أَدْخُلَ. جِئْتُ لِأَدْعُوَكَ إِلَى حَفْلَةِ عِيدِ مِيلَادِ وَلَدِي آدَم يَوْمَ السَّبْت.
npc.en: Thank you, I won't come in. I've come to invite you to my son Adam's birthday party on Saturday.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة! كُلُّ عَامٍ وَهُوَ بِخَيْر. كَمْ عُمْرُهُ الْآنَ؟
choices.en: Thank you for the invitation! Happy birthday to him. How old is he now?
segs: well ('kullu ʿāmin wa-huwa bi-khayr': happy birthday to him)
choices.feedback: Good: كُلُّ عَامٍ وَهُوَ بِخَيْر wishes Adam a happy birthday, and عُمْرُهُ (his age) asks about him.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة! كُلُّ عَامٍ وَهُوَ بِخَيْر. كَمْ عُمْرُهَا الْآنَ؟
choices.en: Thank you for the invitation! Happy birthday to him. How old is she now? (wrong ending)
segs: well ('kullu ʿāmin wa-huwa bi-khayr': happy birthday to him)
choices.feedback: عُمْرُهَا means 'her age'. Adam is a boy: كَمْ عُمْرُهُ الْآنَ؟

npc.ar: سَيَكُونُ عُمْرُهُ سِتَّ سَنَوَات. الْحَفْلَة فِي الْحَدِيقَة أَمَامَ الْبِنَايَة، فِي السَّاعَة الْخَامِسَة.
npc.en: He'll be six years old. The party is in the garden in front of the building, at five o'clock.

choices.ar: يَوْمَ السَّبْت فِي السَّاعَة الْخَامِسَة؟ لَا مُشْكِلَة، لَنْ أَكُونَ مَشْغُولًا. سَآتِي بِكُلِّ سُرُور.
choices.en: Saturday at five? No problem, I won't be busy. I'll come with pleasure.
choices.feedback: Good: the future negative is لَنْ + the verb in -a (لَنْ أَكُونَ), and مَشْغُولًا takes -an after 'be'.

choices.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة، لَا سَأَكُونُ مَشْغُولًا. سَآتِي بِكُلِّ سُرُور.
choices.en: No problem, I won't be busy. I'll come with pleasure. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: Arabic never puts لَا before sa-. The future negative is لَنْ + the verb in -a: لَنْ أَكُونَ مَشْغُولًا.

npc.ar: رَائِع! سَيَكُونُ هُنَاكَ أَطْفَال كَثِيرُونَ مِنَ الْبِنَايَة، وَكَعْكَة كَبِيرَة طَبْعًا.
npc.en: Wonderful! There will be lots of children from the building, and a big cake of course.

choices.ar: هَلْ أُحْضِرُ شَيْئًا؟ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ هَدِيَّة لِآدَم. مَاذَا يُحِبُّ؟
choices.en: Shall I bring something? I'd like to buy a present for Adam. What does he like?
choices.feedback: Good: asking what the child likes is a kind way to choose a present, and يُحِبُّ (yu-) is about Adam.

choices.ar: سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوق غَدًا لِأَشْتَرِيَ هَدِيَّة لِآدَم.
choices.en: I'll go to the market tomorrow to buy a present for Adam.
choices.feedback: Good: after لِ (in order to) the verb ends in -a: لِأَشْتَرِيَ.

choices.ar: هَلْ أُحْضِرُ شَيْئًا؟ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ هَدِيَّة لِآدَم. مَاذَا تُحِبِّينَ؟
choices.en: Shall I bring something? I'd like to buy a present for Adam. What do you like? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: تُحِبِّينَ asks what Suad likes. The present is for Adam: مَاذَا يُحِبُّ؟ (what does he like?)

npc.ar: هُوَ يُحِبُّ كُرَةَ الْقَدَم كَثِيرًا، لٰكِنْ لَا تَشْتَرِ شَيْئًا غَالِيًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ!
npc.en: He loves football, but please don't buy anything expensive!

choices.ar: إِذًا سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوق غَدًا لِأَشْتَرِيَ لَهُ كُرَة صَغِيرَة.
choices.en: Then I'll go to the market tomorrow to buy him a small ball.
choices.feedback: Good: a small ball is cheap and fits what he likes. كُرَة is feminine, so صَغِيرَة.

choices.ar: إِذًا سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوق غَدًا لِأَشْتَرِيَ لَهُ كُرَة صَغِير.
choices.en: Then I'll go to the market tomorrow to buy him a small ball. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: كُرَة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة too: كُرَة صَغِيرَة.

npc.ar: فِكْرَة جَمِيلَة! سَيَفْرَحُ كَثِيرًا. إِذًا نَرَاكَ يَوْمَ السَّبْت.
npc.en: What a lovely idea! He'll be very happy. So we'll see you on Saturday.

choices.ar: إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه. شُكْرًا مَرَّةً أُخْرَى، وَمَعَ السَّلَامَة يَا سَيِّدَة سُعَاد!
choices.en: God willing. Thank you again, and goodbye, Mrs Suad!
choices.feedback: Good: إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه is the usual answer to a plan for the future.

choices.ar: إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه. شُكْرًا مَرَّةً أُخْرَى، وَمَعَ السَّلَامَة يَا سَيِّد سُعَاد!
choices.en: God willing. Thank you again, and goodbye, Mr Suad! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: سَيِّد is 'Mr'. Suad is a woman: يَا سَيِّدَة سُعَاد.

npc.ar: يَا فَيْصَل، مَا رَأْيُكَ؟ نِهَايَةَ الْأُسْبُوع الْقَادِم سَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْبَحْر فِي الْعَيْن السُّخْنَة!
npc.en: Faisal, what do you think? Next weekend we'll go to the sea at Ain Sokhna!
segs: Ain (part of the place name; lit. the spring)
Sokhna (Ain Sokhna: a beach town on the Red Sea)

choices.ar: فِكْرَة رَائِعَة! لٰكِنْ فِي نُوفَمْبِر، هَلْ سَيَكُونُ الْجَوّ دَافِئًا عَلَى الْبَحْر؟
choices.en: A great idea! But in November, will the weather be warm by the sea?
choices.feedback: Good: فِكْرَة is feminine (رَائِعَة), and after سَيَكُونُ the description takes -an: دَافِئًا.

choices.ar: فِكْرَة رَائِع! لٰكِنْ فِي نُوفَمْبِر، هَلْ سَيَكُونُ الْجَوّ دَافِئًا عَلَى الْبَحْر؟
choices.en: A great idea! But in November, will the weather be warm by the sea? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: فِكْرَة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة too: فِكْرَة رَائِعَة.

npc.ar: عَادَةً نَعَم، فَالْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر دَافِئ فِي الْخَرِيف. لٰكِنْ سَأَنْظُرُ إِلَى نَشْرَةِ الطَّقْس فِي هَاتِفِي أَوَّلًا.
npc.en: Usually, yes: the Red Sea is warm in autumn. But I'll look at the weather forecast on my phone first.

choices.ar: حَسَنًا. كَيْفَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة؟
choices.en: All right. What will the weather be like on Friday?
choices.feedback: Good: كَيْفَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس؟ is the standard way to ask about the forecast.

choices.ar: حَسَنًا. كَيْفَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس يَوْمَ السَّبْت؟
choices.en: All right. What will the weather be like on Saturday?
choices.feedback: Good: Saturday instead of Friday. يَوْمَ (on the day of) ends in -a because it says when.

choices.ar: حَسَنًا. أَيْنَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة؟
choices.en: All right. Where will the weather be on Friday? (wrong question word)
choices.feedback: أَيْنَ means 'where'. To ask what the weather will be like, use كَيْفَ: كَيْفَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس؟

npc.ar: يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة سَتَكُونُ هُنَاكَ رِيَاح قَوِيَّة، وَرُبَّمَا تُمْطِرُ قَلِيلًا. هٰذَا غَرِيب فِي مِصْر!
npc.en: On Friday there will be strong winds, and it might rain a little. That's strange in Egypt!

choices.ar: رِيَاح وَمَطَر؟ إِذًا لَنْ نَسْبَحَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة. وَيَوْمَ السَّبْت؟
choices.en: Wind and rain? Then we won't swim on Friday. And what about Saturday?
choices.feedback: Good: the future negative is لَنْ + the verb in -a: لَنْ نَسْبَحَ.

choices.ar: رِيَاح وَمَطَر؟ إِذًا لَا سَنَسْبَحُ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة.
choices.en: Wind and rain? Then we won't swim on Friday. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: The future negative is لَنْ + the verb in -a, never لَا + sa-: لَنْ نَسْبَحَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة.

npc.ar: يَوْمَ السَّبْت سَيَكُونُ الْجَوّ مُشْمِسًا وَدَافِئًا، وَدَرَجَةُ الْحَرَارَة سِتٌّ وَعِشْرُونَ.
npc.en: On Saturday it will be sunny and warm, and the temperature will be twenty-six degrees.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز! إِذًا سَنَذْهَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْت. مَتَى سَنَخْرُجُ مِنَ الْقَاهِرَة؟
choices.en: Excellent! So we'll go on Saturday. When will we leave Cairo?
segs: we will go out, we will leave
choices.feedback: Good: sa- + the present makes the future: سَنَذْهَبُ، سَنَخْرُجُ.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز! إِذًا ذَهَبْنَا يَوْمَ السَّبْت.
choices.en: Excellent! So we went on Saturday. (wrong tense)
choices.feedback: ذَهَبْنَا is the past ('we went'), but the trip is still to come. For the future use sa- + the present: إِذًا سَنَذْهَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْت.

npc.ar: سَنَخْرُجُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة صَبَاحًا لِنَصِلَ قَبْلَ الظُّهْر، فَالطَّرِيق طَوِيل.
npc.en: We'll leave at six in the morning so that we arrive before noon, because the road is long.
segs: we will go out, we will leave

choices.ar: وَمَاذَا نَأْخُذُ مَعَنَا؟ أَنَا لَا أَعْرِفُ الْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر.
choices.en: And what should we take with us? I don't know the Red Sea at all.
choices.feedback: Good: لَا + the present says 'not' now: لَا أَعْرِفُ (I don't know).

choices.ar: وَمَاذَا نَأْخُذُ مَعَنَا؟ أَنَا لَا أَعْرِفُ الْبَحْر الْحَمْرَاء.
choices.en: And what should we take with us? I don't know the Red Sea at all. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: بَحْر is masculine, so the colour is masculine too: الْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر.

npc.ar: خُذْ قُبَّعَةً وَمَاءً كَثِيرًا، لِأَنَّ الشَّمْس قَوِيَّة هُنَاكَ. وَخُذْ مِعْطَفًا خَفِيفًا لِلْمَسَاء.
npc.en: Take a hat and lots of water, because the sun is strong there. And take a light jacket for the evening.

choices.ar: اِتَّفَقْنَا! سَأَشْتَرِي قُبَّعَة جَدِيدَة غَدًا. لَنْ أَنْسَى الْمَاء هٰذِهِ الْمَرَّة!
choices.en: Agreed! I'll buy a new hat tomorrow. I won't forget the water this time!
choices.feedback: Good: قُبَّعَة is feminine, so جَدِيدَة, and لَنْ أَنْسَى is the future negative.

choices.ar: اِتَّفَقْنَا! سَأَشْتَرِي قُبَّعَة جَدِيد غَدًا.
choices.en: Agreed! I'll buy a new hat tomorrow. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: قُبَّعَة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة too: قُبَّعَة جَدِيدَة.

npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! إِلَى أَيْنَ تُسَافِرُ الْيَوْمَ؟ جَوَازُ السَّفَر وَالتَّذْكِرَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
npc.en: Good evening! Where are you flying to today? Your passport and ticket, please.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. أُسَافِرُ إِلَى الْقَاهِرَة. تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذَا جَوَازُ سَفَرِي.
choices.en: Good evening. I'm flying to Cairo. Here you are, this is my passport.
choices.feedback: Good: his تُسَافِرُ (you travel) becomes your أُسَافِرُ (I travel), and تَفَضَّلْ hands the passport to a man.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. أُسَافِرُ إِلَى الْقَاهِرَة. تَفَضَّلِي، هٰذَا جَوَازُ سَفَرِي.
choices.en: Good evening. I'm flying to Cairo. Here you are (to a woman), this is my passport. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: تَفَضَّلِي is said to a woman. The clerk is a man: تَفَضَّلْ.

npc.ar: شُكْرًا. ضَعْ حَقِيبَتَكَ عَلَى الْمِيزَان، لَوْ سَمَحْتَ… وَزْنُهَا ثَلَاثُونَ كِيلُو!
npc.en: Thank you. Put your suitcase on the scales, please… It weighs thirty kilos!
segs: your bag, your suitcase (to a man)

choices.ar: ثَلَاثُونَ؟! هَلْ هٰذَا أَكْثَرُ مِنَ الْمَسْمُوح؟ فِيهَا هَدَايَا كَثِيرَة لِأَصْدِقَائِي فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
choices.en: Thirty?! Is that more than is allowed? There are lots of presents in it for my friends in Cairo.
choices.feedback: Good: هَدَايَا is a plural of things, so its adjective is feminine singular: هَدَايَا كَثِيرَة.

choices.ar: ثَلَاثُونَ؟! هَلْ هٰذَا أَكْثَرُ مِنَ الْمَسْمُوح؟ فِيهَا هَدَايَا كَثِير لِأَصْدِقَائِي فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
choices.en: Thirty?! Is that more than is allowed? There are lots of presents in it for my friends in Cairo. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: A plural of things takes a feminine singular adjective: هَدَايَا كَثِيرَة, not كَثِير.

npc.ar: نَعَم، الْمَسْمُوح ثَلَاثَة وَعِشْرُونَ كِيلُو فَقَطْ. يَجِبُ أَنْ تَدْفَعَ عَنْ كُلِّ كِيلُو زِيَادَة.
npc.en: Yes, the limit is only twenty-three kilos. You have to pay for every extra kilo.

choices.ar: كَمْ أَدْفَعُ؟ وَهَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ آخُذَ بَعْضَ الْأَشْيَاء مَعِي فِي حَقِيبَةِ الْيَد؟
choices.en: How much do I pay? And is it possible to take some things with me in my hand luggage?
choices.feedback: Good: هَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ …؟ is a polite way to ask, and after أَنْ the verb ends in -a: آخُذَ.

choices.ar: كَمْ أَدْفَعُ؟ وَهَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ آخُذُ بَعْضَ الْأَشْيَاء مَعِي فِي حَقِيبَةِ الْيَد؟
choices.en: How much do I pay? And is it possible to take some things with me in my hand luggage? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: After أَنْ the verb ends in -a, not -u: أَنْ آخُذَ.

npc.ar: مُمْكِن. حَقِيبَةُ الْيَد حَتَّى سَبْعَة كِيلُو. أَوْ تَدْفَعُ عَشَرَةَ دَنَانِير عَنْ كُلِّ كِيلُو.
npc.en: It's possible. Hand luggage can be up to seven kilos. Or you pay ten dinars for every kilo.

choices.ar: عَشَرَةُ دَنَانِير لِكُلِّ كِيلُو؟ هٰذَا أَغْلَى مِنَ الْهَدَايَا! لَحْظَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Ten dinars a kilo? That's more expensive than the presents! One moment, please.
choices.feedback: Good: 'more expensive than' is أَغْلَى مِنْ, and لَحْظَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ asks politely for a moment.

choices.ar: أَخَذْتُ الْكُتُب وَالْكُوفِيَّة مِنَ الْحَقِيبَة. هَلْ وَزْنُهَا الْآنَ أَقَلُّ؟
choices.en: I've taken the books and the keffiyeh out of the suitcase. Does it weigh less now?
choices.feedback: Good: you move things into your hand luggage at once. وَزْنُهَا uses -hā because حَقِيبَة is feminine.

choices.ar: عَشَرَةُ دَنَانِير لِكُلِّ كِيلُو؟ هٰذَا غَالٍ مِنَ الْهَدَايَا!
choices.en: Ten dinars a kilo? That's expensive from the presents! (wrong form)
choices.feedback: غَالٍ (expensive) does not compare. 'More expensive than' is أَغْلَى مِنْ: هٰذَا أَغْلَى مِنَ الْهَدَايَا.

npc.ar: طَبْعًا، تَفَضَّلْ.
npc.en: Of course, go ahead.

choices.ar: أَخَذْتُ الْكُتُب وَالْكُوفِيَّة مِنَ الْحَقِيبَة. هَلْ وَزْنُهَا الْآنَ أَقَلُّ؟
choices.en: I've taken the books and the keffiyeh out of the suitcase. Does it weigh less now?
choices.feedback: Good: أَخَذْتُ (-tu) is 'I took', and أَقَلُّ (less) is the comparative of قَلِيل.

choices.ar: أَخَذْتَ الْكُتُب وَالْكُوفِيَّة مِنَ الْحَقِيبَة. هَلْ وَزْنُهَا الْآنَ أَقَلُّ؟
choices.en: You've taken the books and the keffiyeh out of the suitcase. Does it weigh less now? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: أَخَذْتَ (-ta) means 'you took'. You did it yourself: أَخَذْتُ (-tu).

npc.ar: نَعَم، الْآنَ ثَلَاثَة وَعِشْرُونَ كِيلُو بِالضَّبْط. مُمْتَاز! تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذِهِ بِطَاقَةُ الصُّعُود.
npc.en: Yes, now it's exactly twenty-three kilos. Excellent! Here you are, this is your boarding pass.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much! Goodbye.
choices.feedback: Good: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا and مَعَ السَّلَامَة, and you keep your presents without paying extra.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا لَكِ! مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Thank you (to a woman)! Goodbye. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: لَكِ (-ki) is for a woman. The clerk is a man: شُكْرًا لَكَ (-ka), or شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.

npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكَ؟
npc.en: Good evening! How can I help you?
segs: I help you (to a man, after an)

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. لَوْ سَمَحْتِ، عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَة. الْمُكَيِّف فِي الْغُرْفَة لَا يَعْمَلُ، وَالْغُرْفَة حَارَّة جِدًّا.
choices.en: Good evening. Excuse me, I have a problem. The air conditioning in the room doesn't work, and the room is very hot.
choices.feedback: Good: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ ends in -ti because Salma is a woman, and حَارَّة takes ة to agree with الْغُرْفَة.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. لَوْ سَمَحْتَ، عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَة. الْمُكَيِّف فِي الْغُرْفَة لَا يَعْمَلُ، وَالْغُرْفَة حَارَّة جِدًّا.
choices.en: Good evening. Excuse me (to a man), I have a problem. The air conditioning in the room doesn't work, and the room is very hot.
choices.feedback: سَمَحْتَ (-ta) is for a man. Salma is a woman: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ، عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَة.

npc.ar: آسِفَة جِدًّا! هَلْ تُرِيدُ غُرْفَة أُخْرَى؟ عِنْدَنَا غُرْفَة أَكْبَرُ وَأَهْدَأُ فِي الطَّابِق الثَّانِي.
npc.en: I'm very sorry! Would you like another room? We have a bigger, quieter room on the second floor.

choices.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ. هَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ أَرَاهَا أَوَّلًا؟
choices.en: Yes, please. Is it possible to see it first?
choices.feedback: Good: أَرَاهَا ends in -hā because غُرْفَة is feminine, and مِنْ فَضْلِكِ takes -ki for Salma.

choices.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ. هَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ أَرَاهُ أَوَّلًا؟
choices.en: Yes, please. Is it possible to see it first? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: غُرْفَة is feminine, so 'it' is -hā: أَرَاهَا, not أَرَاهُ.

npc.ar: طَبْعًا. تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذَا مِفْتَاحُ الْغُرْفَة رَقْم خَمْسَة فِي الطَّابِق الثَّانِي. الْمِصْعَد عَلَى الْيَسَار.
npc.en: Of course. Here you are, this is the key to room number five on the second floor. The lift is on the left.

choices.ar: الْغُرْفَة الْجَدِيدَة أَفْضَلُ بِكَثِير، وَالْمُكَيِّف يَعْمَلُ. شُكْرًا! سُؤَال آخَر: أَيْنَ نَأْكُلُ الْعَشَاء؟
choices.en: The new room is much better, and the air conditioning works. Thank you! Another question: where can we have dinner?
choices.feedback: Good: أَفْضَلُ (better) keeps one form, even with a feminine noun like الْغُرْفَة.

choices.ar: الْغُرْفَة الْجَدِيدَة أَفْضَلُ بِكَثِير، شُكْرًا! وَأَرْجُو أَنْ تَطْلُبِي لَنَا تَاكْسِي غَدًا فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف.
choices.en: The new room is much better, thank you! And please order us a taxi tomorrow at half past six.
segs: you order (to a woman, after an)
choices.feedback: Good: after أَرْجُو أَنْ, the verb for a woman is تَطْلُبِي, with no final n.

choices.ar: الْغُرْفَة الْجَدِيد أَفْضَلُ بِكَثِير، وَالْمُكَيِّف يَعْمَلُ.
choices.en: The new room is much better, and the air conditioning works. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: الْغُرْفَة is feminine, so its adjective takes ة: الْغُرْفَة الْجَدِيدَة.

npc.ar: مَطْعَمُ الْفُنْدُق مَفْتُوح حَتَّى السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة، وَهُوَ أَرْخَصُ مِنْ مَطَاعِمِ الْمَدِينَة.
npc.en: The hotel restaurant is open until ten o'clock, and it's cheaper than the restaurants in town.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز. وَأَرْجُو أَنْ تَطْلُبِي لَنَا تَاكْسِي غَدًا فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف إِلَى مَدْخَلِ الْبَتْرَاء.
choices.en: Excellent. And please order us a taxi tomorrow at half past six to the entrance of Petra.
segs: you order (to a woman, after an)
choices.feedback: Good: تَطْلُبِي is the form for a woman after أَنْ, and غَدًا carries -an as an adverb.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز. وَأَرْجُو أَنْ تَطْلُبَ لَنَا تَاكْسِي غَدًا فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف إِلَى مَدْخَلِ الْبَتْرَاء.
choices.en: Excellent. And please order us a taxi tomorrow at half past six to the entrance of Petra (to a man).
segs: you order (to a man, after an)
choices.feedback: تَطْلُبَ is for a man. Salma is a woman: أَرْجُو أَنْ تَطْلُبِي لَنَا تَاكْسِي.

npc.ar: بِكُلِّ سُرُور. التَّاكْسِي يَنْتَظِرُكُمْ أَمَامَ الْفُنْدُق، وَالْفُطُور يَبْدَأُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة.
npc.en: With pleasure. The taxi will wait for you in front of the hotel, and breakfast starts at six o'clock.
segs: it waits for you (to several people)

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا عَلَى الْمُسَاعَدَة! تُصْبِحِينَ عَلَى خَيْر.
choices.en: Thank you very much for your help! Good night.
choices.feedback: Good: تُصْبِحِينَ عَلَى خَيْر is 'good night' to a woman.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا عَلَى الْمُسَاعَدَة! تُصْبِحُ عَلَى خَيْر.
choices.en: Thank you very much for your help! Good night (to a man).
choices.feedback: تُصْبِحُ عَلَى خَيْر is said to a man. To Salma: تُصْبِحِينَ عَلَى خَيْر.

npc.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا يَا لَيْلَى، تَفَضَّلِي اجْلِسِي. أَنَا سَلْوَى، مُدِيرَةُ الْمَرْكَز.
npc.en: Welcome, Layla, please have a seat. I'm Salwa, the director of the centre.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا. هٰذِهِ سِيرَتِي الذَّاتِيَّة وَشَهَادَتِي مِنَ الْجَامِعَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much. Here are my CV and my degree certificate from the university.
choices.feedback: Good: هٰذِهِ (f) goes with سِيرَتِي, a feminine noun.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا. هٰذَا سِيرَتِي الذَّاتِيَّة.
choices.en: Thank you very much. Here is my CV. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: The word for CV (sīra) is feminine, so 'this' is هٰذِهِ: هٰذِهِ سِيرَتِي الذَّاتِيَّة.

npc.ar: قَرَأْتُ السِّيرَة الذَّاتِيَّة. أَنْتِ مِنْ لُبْنَان، وَتَدْرُسِينَ فِي الْقَاهِرَة الْآنَ، صَحِيح؟
npc.en: I've read the CV. You're from Lebanon, and you're studying in Cairo now, right?

choices.ar: صَحِيح. أَدْرُسُ فِي مَدْرَسَةِ لُغَة، وَأُسَاعِدُ زُمَلَائِي الْأَجَانِب فِي الْعَرَبِيَّة كُلَّ يَوْم.
choices.en: That's right. I study at a language school, and I help my foreign classmates with Arabic every day.
choices.feedback: Good: you confirm with صَحِيح and add what you do now, in the present tense (أَدْرُسُ، أُسَاعِدُ).

choices.ar: صَحِيح. أَنَا لُبْنَانِيّ، وَأَدْرُسُ فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
choices.en: That's right. I'm Lebanese, and I study in Cairo. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: Layla is a woman, so she says لُبْنَانِيَّة, with ة: أَنَا لُبْنَانِيَّة.

npc.ar: جَمِيل. هَلْ عِنْدَكِ خِبْرَة فِي التَّعْلِيم؟
npc.en: Lovely. Do you have any experience in teaching?

choices.ar: نَعَم، فِي بَيْرُوت عَلَّمْتُ الْأَطْفَال الْعَرَبِيَّة سَنَتَيْنِ.
choices.en: Yes, in Beirut I taught Arabic to children for two years.
choices.feedback: Good: سَنَتَيْنِ (two years) tells how long, so the dual ends in -ayni.

choices.ar: نَعَم، فِي بَيْرُوت عَلَّمْتُ الْأَطْفَال الْعَرَبِيَّة سَنَتَانِ.
choices.en: Yes, in Beirut I taught Arabic to children for two years. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: Here 'two years' tells how long, so the dual takes -ayni: سَنَتَيْنِ, not سَنَتَانِ.

npc.ar: مُمْتَاز. يُمْكِنُنَا أَنْ نُعْطِيَكِ صَفًّا صَغِيرًا مَسَاءَ الْأَحَد وَالثُّلَاثَاء.
npc.en: Excellent. We can give you a small class on Sunday and Tuesday evenings.
segs: we can (lit. it is possible for us)
we give you (to a woman, after an)

choices.ar: هٰذَا مُنَاسِب لِي. وَمَتَى يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أَبْدَأَ؟
choices.en: That suits me. And when can I start?
segs: it is possible for me, I can
choices.feedback: Good: after يُمْكِنُنِي come أَنْ and a verb ending in -a: أَنْ أَبْدَأَ.

choices.ar: هٰذَا مُنَاسِب لِي. وَمَا الرَّاتِب، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ؟
choices.en: That suits me. And what is the salary, please?
choices.feedback: Good: a polite, direct question; مِنْ فَضْلِكِ takes -ki for Mrs Salwa.

choices.ar: هٰذَا مُنَاسِب لِي. وَمَتَى يُمْكِنُنِي أَبْدَأُ؟
choices.en: That suits me. And when can I I start? (wrong form)
segs: it is possible for me, I can
choices.feedback: After يُمْكِنُنِي use أَنْ and a verb ending in -a: مَتَى يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أَبْدَأَ؟

npc.ar: الْأُسْبُوعَ الْقَادِم، إِذَا كُنْتِ مُسْتَعِدَّة.
npc.en: Next week, if you're ready.

choices.ar: أَنَا مُسْتَعِدَّة تَمَامًا! وَمَا الرَّاتِب، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ؟
choices.en: I'm completely ready! And what is the salary, please?
choices.feedback: Good: a woman says مُسْتَعِدَّة, and تَمَامًا carries -an as an adverb.

choices.ar: أَنَا مُسْتَعِدّ تَمَامًا! وَمَا الرَّاتِب، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ؟
choices.en: I'm completely ready! And what is the salary, please? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: A woman says مُسْتَعِدَّة, with ة: أَنَا مُسْتَعِدَّة تَمَامًا.

npc.ar: مِئَتَا جُنَيْه لِكُلِّ دَرْس. وَسَأُرْسِلُ لَكِ الْعَقْد بِالْبَرِيدِ الْإِلِكْتُرُونِيّ الْيَوْم.
npc.en: Two hundred pounds for each lesson. And I'll send you the contract by email today.
segs: by the post, by the mail

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا سَيِّدَة سَلْوَى! أَنَا سَعِيدَة جِدًّا بِهٰذِهِ الْوَظِيفَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much, Mrs Salwa! I'm very happy with this job.
choices.feedback: Good: in an interview the title يَا سَيِّدَة سَلْوَى keeps it formal, and سَعِيدَة agrees with Layla.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا سَلْوَى! أَنَا سَعِيدَة جِدًّا بِهٰذِهِ الْوَظِيفَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much, Salwa! I'm very happy with this job.
choices.feedback: The first name alone is too familiar for the director in an interview. Use the title: يَا سَيِّدَة سَلْوَى.

npc.ar: آلُو، مَكْتَبُ كُلِّيَّةِ الْآدَاب، صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر.
npc.en: Hello, Faculty of Arts office, good morning.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. اِسْمِي فَيْصَل، وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أَسْأَلَ عَنْ مُحَاضَرَاتِ الدُّكْتُورَة مُنَى.
choices.en: Good morning. My name is Faisal, and I'd like to ask about Dr Mona's lectures.
choices.feedback: Good: صَبَاحُ النُّور answers صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر, and أَنْ أَسْأَلَ joins the two verbs.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ أَسْأَلُ عَنْ مُحَاضَرَاتِ الدُّكْتُورَة مُنَى.
choices.en: Good morning. I want I ask about Dr Mona's lectures. (wrong form)
